correctness.rationale: For uniform length-n Motzkin excursions, the first-return equation M=1+wzM+z²(M+v-1)M correctly marks each H and each adjacent UD peak; ground horizontals are separated by F=M/[1-(u-1)wzM]. Differentiating yields exact six moment series M, R=zM², P=z²M/sqrt((1-3z)(1+z)), RP=2z³M²/sqrt(Delta), H=zM/sqrt(Delta), RH=zM²+2z²M²/sqrt(Delta). Singularity transfer at unique dominant 1/3 through second relative correction cancels order n and order 1 in Cov(R,P), leaving -1/n+O(n^-2), while Cov(R,H)=2+O(n^-1). Independently enumerated all paths of lengths 0..11 and checked definitions; n>=5 exact computed RP covariance is negative. The supplied symbolic finite checker has the full transfer coefficient table; infinite asymptotics rely on formal singularity analysis, not the finite test.
residual_risks: The O(n^-2) remainder relies on the stated standard transfer expansion; no finite-n universal negativity is asserted.

value.rationale: Boundary–bulk covariance between ground-level horizontal steps and strict local UD peaks is a natural dependence statistic on uniform Motzkin excursions. The cancellation of leading n and constant terms leaves a sharp negative -1/n interaction, contrasted with a positive limit 2 for global horizontal counts. The exact coefficient is a meaningful second-order benchmark, not a routine one-statistic mean or arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: The theorem is restricted to uncolored uniform Motzkin excursions and not a general covariance limit theorem.
